# Simple Game Factory: Studio website

This repo builds part of Simple Game Factory. The business is defined in its blueprint, and this file is the slice of it this repo needs. Decisions here are settled outside the code: build to them, and when the code shows one is wrong, raise it in the blueprint instead of working around it.

## What this repo is

## Why it exists

Both stores need a privacy link that loads before they review a build. The games share one privacy page and one support page on the studio's own site (`code-publisher-awesoon`, 2026-11-04).

## What it owns

- `www.awesoontechnologies.com/games/privacy`: the v1 policy now, the v2 policy before any ads build ships.
- `www.awesoontechnologies.com/games/support`, with games@awesoontechnologies.com as the contact.
- One landing page per game under `games/<slug>`, built from each game's website page brief (`listing-profile-per-game`).
- `app-ads.txt` at the domain root, one file for every game, before the first ads build (`research/ad-monetization-accounts-2026-11-07.md`).

## What it must never do

- Change what the policy says without a decision behind it; the policy text follows `privacy-v1-collects-nothing` and `privacy-v2-with-ads`.
- Add tracking or analytics to the games pages that the policy does not declare.
- Show a personal contact address.

## Decisions this repo builds

### Published as Awesoon Technologies (`publisher-awesoon`, decided)

Why: one publisher name across ten games builds a studio identity and keeps one policy, one support page and one developer account.

What: copyright reads "2026 Awesoon Technologies". Identifiers are `com.awesoontechnologies.<game>` on both stores. The shared privacy and support pages sit at `www.awesoontechnologies.com/games/privacy` and `/games/support`. Their contact is games@awesoontechnologies.com, a studio address rather than a personal one, set before the first submission (founder, 2026-11-03). The Apple Developer account is a paid team account, separate from the founder's other businesses' Expo account.

One-way because bundle identifiers cannot change after a store listing exists.

Awesoon Technologies is an active British Columbia corporation, restored to the register (founder, 2026-11-04). Ownership and tax setup stay open in `entity-and-tax`.

Sources: repo:SUBMISSION-RUNBOOK.md; repo:app-03-tidy-tiles/store.config.json; repo:legal/privacy-policy.md

### Privacy in 1.0.0: nothing collected (`privacy-v1-collects-nothing`, decided)

Why: with no ads, analytics, account or server, the honest answer to both stores is that nothing is collected.

What: one shared privacy policy (v1) for all ten games says no personal data is collected and everything stays on the device. App Store privacy is answered "No, we do not collect data from this app"; Play Data Safety is answered the same way. Export compliance is answered as no non-exempt encryption.

Outside sign-off: both stores require a reachable privacy policy URL and check it at review. The page exists in the repo but is not yet live (see `privacy-pages-live`).

Not legal advice.

Sources: repo:legal/privacy-policy.md; repo:app-03-tidy-tiles/store/listing.md; repo:SUBMISSION-RUNBOOK.md

### Each repo starts when its outside gate pulls it (`repo-gates-and-timing`, decided)

Why: most work in both repos is pulled by someone outside the company; building ahead of them builds what a reviewer may reject.

`studio-website` has no reviewer of its own. The privacy page loads before any store submission (both stores require it, `rules/text/store-listing-fields.md`). The v2 policy and `app-ads.txt` go live before the first 1.1.0; AdMob verifies the file only once a game is live with the site in its listing. Per-game pages follow each game's pass.

`ten-apps` waits on Apple and Google Play review for every build, plus Play's 12-tester, 14-day test if the account is personal. Ads code starts after `child-audience-and-ads` closes and AdMob approves each app; the dementia folder after `dementia-games-claims` closes. Game order stays in `release-sequence`.

Passed on: building ads and dementia code now; waiting on every gate before any code.

Sources: rules/text/store-listing-fields.md; https://support.google.com/admob/answer/9363762; https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/14151465; research/ad-monetization-accounts-2026-11-07.md

## Other decisions it must respect

`*` marks proposed, not yet confirmed by the founder.

- `accounts-under-corporation`: Apple, Google Play and AdMob accounts are all held by Awesoon Technologies, one D-U-N-S number.
- `age-screen-ads`: Ads build asks birth month and year once; under 13 get kid-safe ads, others choose.
- `all-ages-players`: Anyone who finds the games plays: kids, adults, older adults; advertisers pay from 1.1.0.
- `content-rating-everyone`: Every game is rated 4+ on iOS and Everyone on Play; questionnaire answers are all none.
- `eu-trader-status`: Trader status declared now on the current address; a business address replaces it at the move.
- `insurance-cover`: No policy at 1.0.0; get a broker quote before 1.1.0 ads, bind before any known claim.
- `listing-profile-per-game`: One profile per game; App Store page, Play listing and website brief all derive from it.
- `market-size-and-ad-yield`: Plan on $0.015 to $0.10 ad revenue per daily player; puzzle is the largest casual genre.
- `message-lines`: Always: the thumb action, offline, no account, your own best. Never: free to play, for kids, ranks.
- `privacy-v2-with-ads`: Ads build asks age once, then tracking or consent for 13 and over, with updated policy.
- `store-copy-claims`: Copy claims only real features: no rankings, health claims, fake praise, or no-ads promises.
- `store-keyword-health-terms`: Drop brain training and cognitive from keywords; keep reaction time, focus, stroop; no causes for scores.
- `terms-and-responsibility`: Apple's standard EULA on iOS; one plain studio terms page; Awesoon answers for the games.

## Still open in the blueprint

Do not decide these in code.

- `breach-duties-scope` (counsel): Which breach laws bind the studio
- `child-audience-and-ads` (counsel): Children, age ratings and ads
- `dementia-games-claims` (counsel): Dementia-friendly games: what we may say and who must sign off
- `dnb-business-address` (external): D-U-N-S record carries a business address, not a home
- `entity-and-tax` (counsel): Company ownership and tax on ad income

## How we build

- Before building, say what the item's `Done when` check predicts and what would prove it wrong. Build the core action first.
- Change one thing per try and note each failure with its why. The design stays fixed; the code moves.
- `DECISION: <decision id> <what the code shows>` when a decision is wrong or missing: it goes to the founder.
- `DESIGN: <screen id> <what the build shows>` when a screen cannot be built as designed: it goes to the project manager, who decides whether Design sees it. Never redesign it in code.
- `LESSON: <what we predicted, and what happened>` when a prediction was wrong.
